one_line: Agent-ready fashion shopping with shared outfit state and personal previews.
what_it_does: Lets shoppers and agents search trusted garments, stage an outfit, and obtain a structured render kit for a private personal concept preview.
leverage_rationale: Structured catalog, look, bag, policy, and render-kit state is materially more reliable than an agent reading scattered commerce UI, especially for exact garment references and selected sizes.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies shared visible Style Studio state and read_look_render_kit returning exact garment images, sizes, layers, and generation brief.
Frame sheet visibly shows storefront, conversational assistant, and assembled look states.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent storefront-to-look workflow and the frame sheet shows multiple product and outfit states, but no explicit tool trace or end-to-end generation result is visible.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
Frame sheet shows ELANE storefront, personalization, assistant interaction, and final look-style state.
impact_rationale: Fashion shoppers have a concrete problem of coordinating garments, sizes, budgets, and confidence before purchase; the private-photo design addresses personalization without sending the photo to the store.
impact_evidence: Pitch and description identify outfit-building friction and privacy-preserving concept preview.
Visible product catalog and outfit-builder states support the stated use case.
creativity_rationale: Combining shared agent-readable shopping state with a private, agent-generated outfit preview is a fresh and memorable commerce interaction.
creativity_evidence: Bring-your-own-agent preview keeps the customer's photo in the agent conversation.
Structured render kit bridges staged commerce items to image generation.
usability_note: The visible storefront and assistant flow appear approachable, though tool invocation is not exposed in the frames.
red_flags: No explicit tool-call trace or transcript; visual evidence shows UI outcomes rather than WebMCP execution.
standouts: Privacy-preserving personal preview and exact garment render kit.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific commerce workflow with credible user value and visible product states.

one_line: Agent-operable salon booking storefront with live availability and human confirmation.
what_it_does: Exposes service search, stylist availability, booking, and booking-status tools directly from a salon web app.
leverage_rationale: Booking requires precise service/date/stylist state and a consequential confirmation boundary; structured browser tools are substantially more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Four described tools cover search, live slots, booking with human confirmation, and status lookup.
Pitch explicitly makes the agent operate the booking flow rather than merely describe it.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is focused and coherent, with clear safety gating, but the packet has no submitted video frames proving the central flow.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repo are reported.
Description names a complete search-to-availability-to-book workflow and UI reactions.
impact_rationale: Customers need help finding suitable salon services and times, while local businesses benefit from reduced booking friction; the fit is direct and credible.
impact_evidence: Specific salon booking audience and search/availability problem are clearly stated.
Human confirmation preserves control over reservations.
creativity_rationale: Agent-mediated local-business booking is a strong practical application but a familiar category with a relatively conventional interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Browser-native agent booking and confirmation boundary are well specified.
Concept follows the recognizable search-check-book pattern.
usability_note: The narrow workflow and confirmation gate should be easy for customers to understand.
red_flags: No frame sheets or transcript submitted, so execution is claimed rather than observed.
advance_reason: High practical value and strong WebMCP leverage despite thin visual evidence.

one_line: Context-aware agent orchestration for choosing creative plans, products, capabilities, and workflows.
what_it_does: Maps a creator's intent, region, eligibility, and machine context to relevant software plans, compatibility information, capabilities, and next actions.
leverage_rationale: Structured context can reduce agent errors across regional pricing, eligibility, system requirements, and product capabilities, though a general agent could obtain much of the information with friction.
leverage_evidence: Description emphasizes structured region, student eligibility, plan contents, requirements, and capabilities.
Use cases span recommendation and action routing rather than a single static lookup.
execution_rationale: The concept is coherent but the packet includes no frame sheets and only broad description, so the central workflow is not demonstrated end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository are reported.

impact_evidence: Specific student-in-India scenario and product compatibility problem are provided.

standouts: Context-rich routing across plans, compatibility, and in-app capabilities.

one_line: WebMCP-accessible health screening flows for agent-guided questionnaires and structured results.
what_it_does: Lets an agent discover screenings, retrieve questions, guide answers, score a screening, and provide crisis resources and protocols.
leverage_rationale: Structured multi-step screening state and scoring are materially safer and more repeatable through tools than UI scraping, though medical interpretation remains appropriately bounded.
leverage_evidence: Five tools cover discovery, question retrieval, scoring, crisis resources, and chat-analysis protocol.
Description explicitly removes copy-paste between AI conversation and screening website.
execution_rationale: The workflow and architecture are clearly described, but no frames or transcript demonstrate the screening completing in practice.
execution_evidence: Cloudflare deployment and document.modelContext registration are stated.
Central discover-guide-score flow is specified.
impact_rationale: Accessible screening guidance addresses a real barrier for people seeking initial mental-health or other screening information, with crisis resources providing an important safety affordance.
impact_evidence: Concrete symptom-to-screening example is given.
Crisis-resource tool and structured result flow are explicitly included.
creativity_rationale: Turning a health screening site into a callable, structured component of an agent conversation is a meaningful interaction innovation, though screening itself is familiar.

usability_note: Conversational guidance can reduce navigation friction, but medical safeguards and clear non-diagnostic messaging are important.
red_flags: No visual evidence; health context requires careful boundaries not observable in packet.
advance_reason: High potential impact and strong structured-agent fit, despite missing demonstration evidence.

one_line: Collaborative travel workspace where people and agents iteratively maintain a shared trip plan.
what_it_does: Allows agents to read trips and create or update activities, accommodations, day plans, tasks, expenses, and comments in a visible editable itinerary.
leverage_rationale: The core product is shared mutable state between human and agent across an iterative planning loop; WebMCP enables reliable structured collaboration that chat-only or UI-driving agents cannot replicate as cleanly.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly describes repeated agent/user refinement using latest shared changes.
Tools cover itinerary entities plus tasks, expenses, and comments in one workspace.
Frame sheets show trip home, timetable, chat, task, and expense views.
execution_rationale: Multiple frame sheets visibly cover the main workspace surfaces and the description presents a coherent editable trip lifecycle, with some end-to-end tool evidence still absent.
execution_evidence: Live demo, public repo, and three frame sheets are reported.
Visible trip, timetable, chat, task, and expense states align with the claimed product scope.
impact_rationale: Travel planning is constraint-heavy and iterative; a shared, human-readable plan gives travelers useful control while benefiting from agent speed.
impact_evidence: Fixed bookings, day plans, expenses, and collaborative revision are concrete travel needs.
Description emphasizes preserving conversation context and human control.
creativity_rationale: The shared editable workspace and explicit back-and-forth human-agent planning model are a fresh, well-pursued alternative to one-shot itinerary generation.
creativity_evidence: Agent is a participant in a living itinerary rather than a one-time generator.
Bring-your-own-agent stance is integrated into the product philosophy.
usability_note: Multiple focused views support understandable collaborative planning, though breadth may increase complexity.
red_flags: Frames show product states but do not clearly expose WebMCP invocation traces.
standouts: Strong shared-state collaboration model across itinerary entities.
advance_reason: Best combination of WebMCP indispensability, coherent scope, and visible collaborative product evidence.

one_line: Cross-device runtime where agents build, run, and hot-swap WebMCP tools as capabilities change.
what_it_does: Combines files, cameras, compute, and human input across devices; routes requests, replans around disconnections, and hot-registers compatible tool versions.
leverage_rationale: The product directly addresses dynamic agent capability composition and cross-device shared state; its intended experience is impractical to reproduce comparably through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description covers compiling a photo-search tool from multiple devices, routing camera requests to a phone, and replanning after disconnection.
Hot-swapping version two under the same name and schema is a core WebMCP-native capability.
execution_rationale: A 179-second video and three frame sheets support a coherent ambitious workflow with visible stages, though detailed tool logs are not available in the packet.
execution_evidence: Video is reported with title and duration; frame sheets are submitted.
Description gives a concrete cross-device compile, human-input, disconnect, and hot-swap sequence.
impact_rationale: People and agents routinely face fragmented devices, private files, sensors, and compute; a living runtime could remove substantial coordination friction for technical and creative workflows.
impact_evidence: Concrete draft/addendum/phone-camera/desktop-GPU scenario is described.
Handles privacy, physical-world input, and device availability.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic cross-device tool synthesis, human participation as a runtime capability, and schema-preserving hot-swapping form an unusually original and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Living runtime metaphor is pursued through compile, route, replan, and hot-register behaviors.
Combines people, agents, and heterogeneous devices rather than adding a single agent endpoint.
usability_note: Powerful for technical users, but capability discovery and cross-device coordination may be complex.
red_flags: Ambitious claims require careful technical validation beyond the supplied packet.
standouts: Most WebMCP-native concept: dynamic capabilities, human routing, and hot-swap resilience.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creativity with unusually strong video-backed ambition.
